meaning: to argue against an idea on purpose, in order to test how strong it is
literal_translation: defender o lado contrário de propósito para testar uma ideia
example: In the seminar, Maria played devil's advocate to check whether our argument would survive criticism.
origin: It comes from the advocatus diaboli, an official of the Catholic Church who argued against the sainthood of a candidate so that the case was examined carefully.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to defend a criminal in court as a lawyer
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is not about legal defence. It describes arguing against an idea during a discussion.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to pretend to be evil in a theatre performance
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with acting or playing a villain. It refers to a debate strategy.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse to take part in any discussion
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes taking a strong opposing position, not avoiding the discussion.

explanation: 'To play devil's advocate' means to deliberately argue against a point of view, even if you do not believe it, so that the group can test and improve the idea.
